PlotMiningMatrix

Source: R/PlotMiningMatrix.R
PlotMiningMatrix.Rd

Generate a matrix of statistical relationships between variables.

Usage

PlotMiningMatrix(
  data,
  outcome_vars,
  predictor_vars = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  Relabel = TRUE,
  TreatOrdinalAs = "Categorical",
  Parametric = TRUE,
  Data = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  OutcomeVars = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  PredictorVars = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  fdr_scope = c("matrix", "per_outcome", "per_predictor"),
  IncludeTrendSymbol = FALSE,
  Covariates = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  Pthresh = 0.05,
  PVar = "PValue"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

outcome_vars

Outcome variables.

predictor_vars

Predictor variables. If NULL, uses OutcomeVars.

covariates

Optional variables to exclude from the tested axes.

Relabel

Use labels instead of names.

TreatOrdinalAs

How ordinal variables are handled: "Categorical", "Continuous", "Both", or "Exclude".

Parametric

Use parametric tests.

Data

Deprecated (since 19.15.0). Use data instead.

OutcomeVars

Deprecated (since 19.15.0). Use outcome_vars instead.

PredictorVars

Deprecated (since 19.15.0). Use predictor_vars instead.

fdr_scope

One of "matrix", "per_outcome", or "per_predictor". Correction uses the symmetrized table before selecting the displayed grid. "matrix" corrects all p-values together (historical behavior). "per_outcome" groups by x-axis outcome (XVar), correcting over predictors; "per_predictor" groups by y-axis predictor (YVar), correcting over outcomes.

IncludeTrendSymbol

Logical; add a plus sign for 0.05 < p <= 0.10. Defaults to FALSE; the trend legend entry is omitted when disabled.

Covariates

Deprecated (since 19.15.0). Use covariates instead.

Pthresh

Significance threshold, default 0.05. An explicitly supplied value takes precedence over a legacy significance threshold argument.

PVar

P-value column used for significance decisions. Defaults to raw "PValue"; select "PValueFDR" to use Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted values. Explicit legacy p-column names remain accepted. Existing, explicitly named FDR plots and adjusted-value columns are retained.

Explicit Pthresh takes precedence over Alpha, FDRAlpha, label_q, or adjusted_significance_threshold. Pairwise star_p = "adjusted" retains its legacy adjustment method unless PVar is supplied; PVar = "PValueFDR" always selects BH. star_p = "none" suppresses legacy pairwise stars. Stars retain conventional p-value tiers within the requested cutoff.

Value

List with tables and plots.

Details

Numeric pairs use Pearson correlation when Parametric = TRUE, and Spearman otherwise. Categorical/numeric pairs use ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis in either orientation; categorical pairs use chi-squared tests. Logical columns are converted locally to FALSE/TRUE factors, preserving labels. Missing effect sizes retain their p-values and plot in neutral grey. Colors represent absolute effect sizes on a fixed 0–1 scale with a square-root transformation to emphasize smaller effects. Values outside these limits are squished to the endpoints for color mapping only; legend labels and returned estimates remain in original effect-size units. Significance uses the p-values selected by PVar: circles for p > 0.05, triangles for 0.01 < p <= 0.05, squares for 0.001 < p <= 0.01, and diamonds for p <= 0.001. With IncludeTrendSymbol = TRUE, plus signs represent 0.05 < p <= 0.10 and circles represent p > 0.10. Marker sizes are fixed across plots: circle 2, plus 2.7, triangle 3.5, square 4, and diamond 6. The legend includes all enabled bands at these sizes. Unadjusted$Missing lists requested non-self pairs without a finite p-value.

Statistical results and provenance

See inference-results for the shared Results and Metadata contract.

Examples

data(SampleData)
data(SampleVariableTypes)

# Attach labels and factor levels for readable axes
Labelled <- RevalueData(SampleData, SampleVariableTypes)$RevaluedData

# A mining matrix over 11 mixed-type variables (categorical + continuous)
result <- PlotMiningMatrix(
  Labelled,
  outcome_vars   = c("Diagnosis", "sex", "age", "AXL", "Adiponectin"),
  predictor_vars = c("Alpha_1_Antitrypsin", "Alpha_2_Macroglobulin",
                     "Apolipoprotein_B", "C_Reactive_Protein",
                     "Cortisol", "Insulin")
)

# The relationship plot (point shape/size encode significance from raw p)
result$Unadjusted$plot


# The p-value table carries both unadjusted (p) and FDR-adjusted (p_adj)
# p-values so results can be inspected with and without FDR correction
result$Unadjusted$PvalTable[, c("XVar", "YVar", "p", "p_adj", "Test")]
#> # A tibble: 30 × 5
#>    XVar        YVar                         p    p_adj Test       
#>    <chr>       <chr>                    <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>      
#>  1 AXL         Alpha_1_Antitrypsin   1.12e- 1 1.87e- 1 Correlation
#>  2 AXL         Alpha_2_Macroglobulin 8.35e-15 8.35e-14 Correlation
#>  3 AXL         Apolipoprotein_B      6.02e- 1 6.95e- 1 Correlation
#>  4 AXL         C_Reactive_Protein    4.82e- 1 6.48e- 1 Correlation
#>  5 AXL         Cortisol              1.85e- 2 4.07e- 2 Correlation
#>  6 AXL         Insulin               2.29e-14 1.71e-13 Correlation
#>  7 Adiponectin Alpha_1_Antitrypsin   1.21e-15 1.82e-14 Correlation
#>  8 Adiponectin Alpha_2_Macroglobulin 3.24e-12 1.95e-11 Correlation
#>  9 Adiponectin Apolipoprotein_B      2.00e-18 6.00e-17 Correlation
#> 10 Adiponectin C_Reactive_Protein    1.02e- 1 1.80e- 1 Correlation
#> # ℹ 20 more rows

# Per-outcome FDR correction instead of matrix-wide
result_perout <- PlotMiningMatrix(
  Labelled,
  outcome_vars   = c("Diagnosis", "sex", "age", "AXL", "Adiponectin"),
  predictor_vars = c("Alpha_1_Antitrypsin", "Alpha_2_Macroglobulin",
                     "Apolipoprotein_B", "C_Reactive_Protein",
                     "Cortisol", "Insulin"),
  fdr_scope = "per_outcome"
)

# An interactive version of the matrix
if (requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)) {
  plotly::ggplotly(result$Unadjusted$plot)
}
